open_points.subject: A1 INV-02 Required tests
open_points.text: a trace of every file the process opens while the delivery runs shows no opening of the named file, of a folder past the segment that fails or of a link's target
open_points.question: When an ignored segment is itself a folder, must the test also show that the failing folder itself was never opened, as INV-02 requires, or only that nothing beyond it was opened?
options: The failing folder itself must not be opened.
Opening the failing folder is allowed, but opening anything beyond it is forbidden.
open_points.default_guess: Validate every name segment first and require the trace to show that neither the failing folder nor anything beyond it was opened.

witness.initial: A confirmed project has an ignored folder `.hidden` containing `photo.jpg`, and the content has no placement.
events: The calling flow requests delivery of `.hidden/photo.jpg`.
One implementation rejects the ignored segment before opening `.hidden`.
Another implementation opens `.hidden` without following links, then rejects before opening `photo.jpg`.
outcomes: The trace contains no opening of `.hidden` or `photo.jpg`.
The trace contains an opening of `.hidden` but not `photo.jpg`; the stated Required tests sentence still forbids only a folder past the failing segment.
witness.observer: The INV-02 witness check inspecting the open trace.

open_points.subject: A2 image validation precedence
open_points.text:
a source it cannot open as one of them is
   `unreadable_image`. Checks run in this order: a first frame above the pixel
   limit (width times height) fails with `too_many_pixels`
open_points.question: What failure applies when the image library refuses while opening an image because its declared first-frame dimensions are excessive: `UNREADABLE_IMAGE` because it could not be opened, or `TOO_MANY_PIXELS` because the dimensions exceed the product limit and that check is listed first?
options: Return `TOO_MANY_PIXELS` whenever excessive dimensions can be obtained from the open result or its failure.
Every failure of the library's open operation is `UNREADABLE_IMAGE`.
Configure or wrap the library so its own size refusal cannot occur before the product pixel-limit check.
open_points.default_guess: Ensure the product pixel-limit check takes precedence and return `TOO_MANY_PIXELS` whenever the dimensions are available; use `UNREADABLE_IMAGE` only when they cannot be established.

witness.initial: A ready source has an allowed signature and declares a first frame above `MAX_PIXELS`; the pinned image library refuses during open because of those dimensions.
events: The calling flow requests its delivery.
One implementation maps the library open failure directly to `UNREADABLE_IMAGE`.
Another extracts or independently obtains the dimensions and applies the stated first check.
witness.observer: The owner receives a different placement failure reason.

open_points.subject: A5 INV-10 Required tests
open_points.text: For an absent file, a file that cannot be opened, a file that is not UTF-8 or JSON, a file of another form and a record that breaks the form of rule 8, also when that record is unconfirmed or belongs to another project, scan, placement and mark each answer the FOLDER_UNAVAILABLE member of = models.RefusalCode and write nothing (`test_unreadable_connections_deliver_nothing`)
open_points.question: Must `test_unreadable_connections_deliver_nothing` explicitly use JSON with a repeated member name—and at which object levels—to demonstrate the newly added rule that a repeated member anywhere breaks the file, or may “a file of another form” be witnessed only by some unrelated schema defect?
options: Include duplicate-member fixtures at every object level permitted by the file shape.
Include at least one duplicate-member fixture.
Treat any existing wrong-form fixture as sufficient without testing duplicate detection.
open_points.default_guess: Add duplicate-member fixtures for the root object, the `objects` map and a connection-entry object, and require all three operations and startup to reject them as specified.
